O Allah, O Thou Who hast shown subtle kindness in creating the heavens and the earth, and shown subtle gentleness to infants in their mothers’ wombs: treat us gently in Thy decree and predestination, with a gentleness worthy of Thy generous nobility, O Most Merciful of the merciful! (Three times)

O Allah, grant victory by Thy bounty unto our authority; destroy the enemies of truth; grant safety in our homelands; appoint over our affairs the best among us, and do not appoint over us the wicked; lift from us Thy indignation and Thy wrath; and do not set over us, on account of our sins, those who do not fear Thee nor show us mercy, O Lord of the Worlds!

audio.title: The Supplication of Completion (دُعَاءُ خَتْمِ دَلَائِلِ الخَيْرَات)

works.source_en: Classical public-domain Arabic text of Imam al-Jazūlī (d. 1465), as circulated in standard editions. English: historical translation by Rev. John B. Pearson (Guide to Happiness, Oxford, 1907), in the public domain globally, covering the Opening Supplication, Intention, Ḥizbs 1–8, and Supplication of Completion. A modern rendering in present-day English, made for this project, appears beneath the Victorian text throughout every section as a reading aid; the Pearson translation remains the citable text.

works.title_en: Ṭalaʿa al-Badru ʿAlaynā (The Full Moon Has Risen)
works.author: The people of Madinah
works.description_en: The welcome sung by the people of Madinah — tradition holds, by its young girls — as the Prophet ﷺ entered the city at the end of the Hijrah, coming over the mountain passes known as the Thaniyyāt al-Wadāʿ, the Passes of Farewell. Perhaps the oldest and most beloved devotional song in Islam.
works.source_en: Traditional text sung at the Prophet’s ﷺ arrival in Madinah, as transmitted in the sīra literature. The English rendering is original to this project.

sections.heading: The Welcome Song
sections.note: Sung at Qubā, on the outskirts of Madinah, in September 622.

units.ar: طَلَعَ الْبَدْرُ عَلَيْنَا — مِنْ ثَنِيَّاتِ الْوَدَاعِ
units.en: The full moon has risen upon us — from the Passes of Farewell;

units.ar: وَجَبَ الشُّكْرُ عَلَيْنَا — مَا دَعَا لِلَّهِ دَاعِ
units.en: and thanks is owed from us — as long as a caller calls to Allah.

units.ar: أَيُّهَا الْمَبْعُوثُ فِينَا — جِئْتَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُطَاعِ
units.en: O you who were sent among us — you came with a command to be obeyed;

units.ar: جِئْتَ شَرَّفْتَ الْمَدِينَةَ — مَرْحَبًا يَا خَيْرَ دَاعٍ
units.en: you came and honoured Madinah — welcome, O best of callers.

works.author: Ḥassān ibn Thābit
works.description_en: Ḥassān ibn Thābit of Madinah was the Prophet’s ﷺ own poet, given a minbar in the mosque from which to answer those who lampooned him — “Jibrīl is with you as long as you defend the Messenger of Allah.” These short pieces are among the most famous madih verses in the language. The two elegies were composed after the Prophet’s ﷺ death in 632.
works.source_en: Arabic texts as transmitted in Ḥassān’s dīwān (following Hirschfeld’s 1910 edition) and, for the minbar poem, in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. The English renderings are original to this project.

sections.heading: The Celebrated Quatrain
sections.note: The most famous lines of prophetic praise in Arabic — Ḥassān’s eyewitness description of the Prophet ﷺ.

units.ar: وَأَحْسَنُ مِنْكَ لَمْ تَرَ قَطُّ عَيْنِي
units.en: My eye has never seen anyone more excellent than you,

units.ar: وَأَجْمَلُ مِنْكَ لَمْ تَلِدِ النِّسَاءُ
units.en: and no woman has ever borne one more beautiful than you;

units.ar: خُلِقْتَ مُبَرَّأً مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ
units.en: you were created free of every fault,

units.ar: كَأَنَّكَ قَدْ خُلِقْتَ كَمَا تَشَاءُ
units.en: as though you were created just as you wished.

sections.heading: The Defence from the Minbar
sections.note: From Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: Ḥassān’s answer, from the minbar set up for him in the mosque, to the poets of Quraysh who lampooned the Prophet ﷺ.

units.ar: هَجَوْتَ مُحَمَّدًا فَأَجَبْتُ عَنْهُ — وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ فِي ذَاكَ الْجَزَاءُ
units.en: You lampooned Muḥammad — and I answered for him; with Allah lies the reward for that.

units.ar: هَجَوْتَ مُحَمَّدًا بَرًّا حَنِيفًا — رَسُولَ اللَّهِ شِيمَتُهُ الْوَفَاءُ
units.en: You lampooned Muḥammad: a righteous, upright man, the Messenger of Allah, whose nature is loyalty.

units.ar: فَإِنَّ أَبِي وَوَالِدَهُ وَعِرْضِي — لِعِرْضِ مُحَمَّدٍ مِنْكُمْ وِقَاءُ
units.en: So my father, my mother, and my honour are a shield for Muḥammad’s honour against you.

units.ar: فَمَنْ يَهْجُو رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مِنْكُمْ — وَيَمْدَحُهُ وَيَنْصُرُهُ سَوَاءُ
units.en: Whoever of you lampoons the Messenger of Allah — or praises him or aids him — it is all the same:

units.ar: وَجِبْرِيلُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ فِينَا — وَرُوحُ الْقُدُسِ لَيْسَ لَهُ كِفَاءُ
units.en: Jibrīl, Allah’s messenger, is among us, and the Holy Spirit has no equal.

sections.heading: The Elegy of Madinah
sections.note: Ḥassān’s lament after the Prophet’s ﷺ death in Madinah in 632 — poem 133 of his dīwān, also transmitted in Ibn Hishām’s Sīra.

units.ar: مَا بَالُ عَيْنِي لَا تَكَادُ كَأَنَّمَا — كُحِلَتْ مَآقِيهَا بِكُحْلِ الْأَرْمَدِ
units.en: What ails my eye? It is all but as though its corners had been lined with the kohl of the sore-eyed,

units.ar: جَزَعًا عَلَى الْمَهْدِيِّ أَضْحَى ثَاوِيًا — يَا خَيْرَ مَنْ وَطِئَ الْحَصَى لَا تَبْعَدِ
units.en: in anguish for the rightly-guided one who now lies in the earth: O best of all who ever trod the gravel, do not be far.

units.ar: جَنْبِي يَقِيكَ الثَّرَى لَهْفِي لَيْتَنِي — غُيِّبْتُ قَبْلَكَ فِي بَقِيعِ الْغَرْقَدِ
units.en: May my side shield you from the soil; alas — would that I had been buried before you in Baqīʿ al-Gharqad.

units.ar: أَأَقِيمُ بَعْدَكَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ بَيْنَهُمْ — يَا لَهْفَ نَفْسِي لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُولَدِ
units.en: Shall I remain in Madinah among them after you? Alas for my soul — would that I had never been born.

units.ar: بِأَبِي وَأُمِّي مَنْ شَهِدْتُ وَفَاتَهُ — فِي يَوْمِ الْإِثْنَيْنِ النَّبِيِّ الْمُهْتَدِي
units.en: May my father and my mother be ransom for the one whose death I witnessed on the Monday: the Prophet, the rightly-guided.

units.ar: فَظَلِلْتُ بَعْدَ وَفَاتِهِ مُتَلَدِّدًا — يَا لَيْتَنِي أُعْطِيتُ سَمَّ الْأَسْوَدِ
units.en: After his passing I remained writhing — would that I had been given the venom of the black viper,

units.ar: أَوْ حَلَّ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ فِينَا عَاجِلًا — مِنْ يَوْمِنَا فِي رَوْحَةٍ أَوْ فِي غَدِ
units.en: or that Allah's decree had fallen on us at once that very day, in an evening or a morning,

units.ar: فَسَقُومُ سَاعَتَنَا فَنَلْقَى طَيِّبًا — مَحْضًا صَرَائِفُهُ كَرِيمَ الْمَحْتِدِ
units.en: then I would rise at our Hour and we would meet the Pure One — unmixed in his character, noble in his origin.

units.ar: يَا بَكْرَ آمِنَةَ الْمُبَارَكُ ذِكْرُهُ — وَلَدَتْكَ مُحْصَنَةٌ بِسَعْدِ الْأَسْعَدِ
units.en: O firstborn of Āmina, blessed is his mention — a chaste woman bore you with the fortune of the most fortunate,

units.ar: نُورًا أَضَاءَ عَلَى الْبَرِيَّةِ كُلِّهَا — مَنْ يُهْدَ لِلنُّورِ الْمُبَارَكِ يَهْتَدِ
units.en: a light that shone out over all creation; whoever is brought to the blessed light is guided aright.

units.ar: يَا رَبِّ فَاجْمَعْنَا مَعًا وَبَوِّئْنَا — فِي جَنَّةٍ تُثْنِي عُيُونَ الْحُسَّادِ
units.en: O Lord, gather us together and settle us in a Garden that turns away the eyes of the envious,

units.ar: فِي جَنَّةِ الْفِرْدَوْسِ وَاكْتُبْهَا لَنَا — يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَذَا الْعُلَا وَالسُّؤْدَدِ
units.en: in the Garden of Firdaws — and write it for us, O Lord of majesty, of sublimity and of dominion.

units.ar: وَاللَّهِ أَسْمَعْ مَا حَيِيتُ بِهَا إِلَهِي — إِلَّا بَكَيْتُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدِ
units.en: By Allah — as long as I live, I hear nothing in Madinah, my God, without weeping for the Prophet Muḥammad.

units.ar: ضَاقَتْ بِالْأَنْصَارِ الْبِلَادُ فَأَصْبَحُوا — سُرًى وُجُوهُهُمْ كُلُّهُمُ الْإِثْمِدِ
units.en: The land grew too narrow for the Anṣār; they became keepers of the night-vigil, all their faces dark as antimony.

units.ar: وَلَقَدْ وَلَدَنَاهُ وَفِينَا قَبِرُهُ — وَفُضُولُ نِعْمَتِهِ بَدَا لِلْعِبَادِ
units.en: Among us he was born, and among us is his grave; and the overflowing of his bounty was plain to all people.

units.ar: صَلَّى اللَّهُ وَمَنْ يَحُفُّ بِعَرْشِهِ — وَالطَّيِّبُونَ عَلَى الْمُبَارَكِ أَحْمَدِ
units.en: May Allah bless — and those who surround His Throne, and the pure ones — the blessed one, Aḥmad.

units.ar: فَرِحَتْ نَصَارَى يَثْرِبَ وَيَهُودُهَا — لَمَّا تُوَارَى فِي الضَّرِيحِ الْمُلْحَدِ
units.en: The Christians of Yathrib and its Jews rejoiced when he was hidden away in the grave’s side-niche.

audio.title: The Elegy of Madinah (Mā Bālu ʿAynī)

sections.heading: The Grand Elegy of Madinah
sections.note: Ḥassān’s greatest and most celebrated lament (Bi-Ṭaybata Rasmun) after the passing of the Prophet ﷺ — poem 134 of his dīwān.

audio.title: The Grand Elegy of Madinah (Bi-Ṭaybata Rasmun)

units.ar: بَطَيبَةَ رَسمٌ لِلرَسولِ وَمَعهَدُ — مُنيرٌ وَقَد تَعفو الرُسومُ وَتَهمَدِ
units.en: In Ṭaybah (Madīnah) there remains a trace and an abode of the Messenger, luminous — though other traces may fade and perish.

units.ar: وَلا تَمتَحي الآياتُ مِن دارِ حُرمَةٍ — بِها مِنبَرُ الهادي الَذي كانَ يَصعَدُ
units.en: The sacred signs of that sanctuary shall never be erased, wherein stands the Minbar of the Guide, which he once ascended.

units.ar: وَواضِحُ آثارٍ وَباقي مَعالِمٍ — وَرَبعٌ لَهُ فيهِ مُصَلّى وَمَسجِدُ
units.en: Clear footprints and enduring landmarks remain, and a courtyard wherein was his prayer place and his masjid.

units.ar: بِها حُجُراتٌ كانَ يَنزِلُ وَسطَها — مِنَ اللَهِ نورٌ يُستَضاءُ وَيوقَدُ
units.en: Therein are chambers into the midst of which used to descend light from Allah, illuminating and kindled.

units.ar: مَعارِفُ لَم تُطمَس عَلى العَهدِ آيُها — أَتاها البِلى فَالآيُ مِنها تُجَدَّدُ
units.en: Signs of knowledge whose verses have not been effaced over time; though decay touches them, their verses are ever renewed.

units.ar: عَرِفتُ بِها رَسمَ الرَسولِ وَعَهدَهُ — وَقَبراً بِها واراهُ في التُربِ مُلحِدُ
units.en: There I recognized the trace of the Messenger and his covenant, and a grave wherein the grave-digger hid him in the earth.

units.ar: ظَلَلتُ بِها أَبكي الرَسولِ فَأَسعَدَت — عُيونٌ وَمِثلاها مِنَ الجِنِّ تُسعَدُ
units.en: There I remained weeping for the Messenger, and eyes helped me in tears, and like them from sorrow were aided.

units.ar: يُذَكِّرنَ آلاءَ الرَسولِ وَما أَرى — لَها مُحصِياً نَفسي فَنَفسي تَبَلَّدُ
units.en: Reminding of the bounties of the Messenger, while my soul can never fully recount them, so my soul grows bewildered.

units.ar: مُفَجَّعَةً قَد شَفَّها فَقدُ أَحمَدٍ — فَظَلَّت لِآلاءِ الرَسولِ تُعَدِّدُ
units.en: Distressed, worn thin by the loss of Aḥmad, she persisted in counting the bounties of the Messenger.

units.ar: وَما بَلَغَت مِن كُلِّ أَمرٍ عَشيرَهُ — وَلَكِن لِنَفسي بَعدُ ما قَد تَوَجَّدُ
units.en: Yet she never attained even a tenth of the whole matter, but within my soul remains sorrow for what has befallen.

units.ar: أَطالَت وُقوفاً تَذرِفُ العَينُ جُهدَها — عَلى طَلَلِ القَبرِ الَذي فيهِ أَحمَدُ
units.en: She stood long, the eye shedding tears to its utmost upon the remains of the grave wherein rests Aḥmad.

units.ar: فَبورِكتَ يا قَبرَ الرَسولِ وَبورِكَت — بِلادٌ ثَوى فيها الرَشيدُ المُسَدَّدُ
units.en: Blessed be you, O grave of the Messenger, and blessed be the land wherein rests the rightly guided, upright master!

units.ar: وَبورِكَ لَحدٌ مِنكَ ضُمِّنَ طَيِّباً — عَلَيهِ بِناءٌ مِن صَفيحٍ مُنَضَّدُ
units.en: And blessed is the niche from you that enclosed one so pure, upon which stands a structure of neatly laid stone slabs!

units.ar: تَهيلُ عَلَيهِ التُربَ أَيدٍ وَأَعيُنٌ — عَلَيهِ وَقَد غارَت بِذَلِكَ أَسعُدُ
units.en: Hands pour earth upon him, and tearful eyes gaze upon him, and by that loss Auspicious stars sank below the horizon.

units.ar: لَقَد غَيَّبوا حِلماً وَعِلماً وَرَحمَةً — عَشِيَّةَ عَلَّوهُ الثَرى لا يُوَسَّدُ
units.en: Indeed, they concealed forbearance, knowledge, and mercy on the evening they covered him with earth, unpillowed.

units.ar: وَراحوا بِحُزنٍ لَيسَ فيهِم نَبيُّهُم — وَقَد وَهَنَت مِنهُم ظُهورٌ وَأَعضُدُ
units.en: And they departed in profound grief, without their Prophet among them, and their backs and forearms were weakened.

units.ar: يُبَكّونَ مَن تَبكي السَمَواتُ يَومَهُ — وَمَن قَد بَكَتهُ الأَرضُ فَالناسُ أَكمَدُ
units.en: They weep for him whose day the heavens weep for, and for whom the earth has wept, so the people are in deep sorrow.

units.ar: وَهَل عَدَلَت يَوماً رَزِيَّةُ هالِكٍ — رَزِيَّةَ يَومٍ ماتَ فيهِ مُحَمَّدُ
units.en: Has the calamity of any mortal ever equaled the calamity of the day on which Muḥammad died?

units.ar: تَقَطَّعَ فيهِ مُنزَلُ الوَحيِ عَنهُمُ — وَقَد كانَ ذا نورٍ يَغورُ وَيُنجِدُ
units.en: On that day the descent of Revelation was severed from them, whereas he was a guiding light illuminating mountain and plain.

units.ar: يَدُلُّ عَلى الرَحمَنِ مَن يَقتَدي بِهِ — وَيُنقِذُ مِن هَولِ الخَزايا وَيُرشِدُ
units.en: Guiding toward the Merciful whoever follows him, rescuing from the terror of disgrace and providing true guidance.

units.ar: إِمامٌ لَهُم يَهديهِمُ الحَقَّ جاهِداً — مُعَلِّمُ صِدقٍ إِن يُطيعوهُ يَسعَدوا
units.en: A leader for them, striving earnestly to guide them to the Truth; a truthful teacher, whom if they obey, they find eternal bliss.

units.ar: عَفُوٌّ عَنِ الزَلّاتِ يَقبَلُ عُذرَهُم — وَإِن يُحسِنوا فَاللَهُ بِالخَيرِ أَجوَدُ
units.en: Forgiving of lapses, accepting their excuses; and if they do good, Allah with goodness is more generous.

units.ar: وَإِن نابَ أَمرٌ لَم يَقوموا بِحَملِهِ — فَمِن عِندِهِ تَيسيرُ ما يَتَشَدَّدُ
units.en: And if a calamity befell them that they could not bear, from him came ease for that which was burdensome.

units.ar: فَبينا هُمُ في نِعمَةِ اللَهِ وَسطَهُم — دَليلٌ بِهِ نَهجُ الطَريقَةِ يُقصَدُ
units.en: And while they were amidst Allah's blessing among them, with a guide through whom the path of the right way is sought,

units.ar: عَزيزٌ عَلَيهِ أَن يَجوروا عَنِ الهُدى — حَريصٌ عَلى أَن يَستَقيموا وَيَهتَدوا
units.en: He grieved that they should deviate from guidance, and was ever anxious that they should stand upright and be guided,

units.ar: عَطوفٌ عَلَيهِم لا يُثَنّي جَناحَهُ — إِلى كَنَفٍ يَحنو عَلَيهِم وَيَمهَدُ
units.en: Compassionate toward them, not folding his protective wing from providing refuge, affection, and gentle care,

units.ar: فَبَينا هُمُ في ذَلِكَ النورِ إِذ غَدا — إِلى نورِهِم سَهمٌ مِنَ المَوتِ مُقصَدُ
units.en: While they were in that brilliant light, suddenly there sped toward their light an aimed arrow of death.

units.ar: فَأَصبَحَ مَحموداً إِلى اللَهِ راجِعاً — يُبكيهِ حَقُّ المُرسِلاتِ وَيُحمَدُ
units.en: So he returned, praised, unto Allah, wept over by the angels of the Holy Revelations, and praised.

units.ar: وَأَمسَت بِلادُ الحُرمَ وَحشاً بِقاعُها — لِغَيبَةِ ما كانَت مِنَ الوَحيِ تَعهَدُ
units.en: And the lands of the Sanctuary became desolate in their tracts, grieving the absence of the Revelation they were accustomed to.

units.ar: قِفاراً سِوى مَعمورَةِ اللَحدِ ضافَها — فَقيدٌ تُبَكّيهِ بَلاطٌ وَغَرقَدُ
units.en: Desolate wastes, save for the inhabited vault of the tomb, visited by the lost one over whom the courtyards and the Baqīʿ weep.

units.ar: وَمَسجِدُهُ فَالموحِشاتُ لِفَقدِهِ — خَلاءٌ لَهُ فيهِ مَقامٌ وَمَقعَدُ
units.en: And his masjid — desolate indeed from his loss — left empty where once he had a station and a seat.

units.ar: وَبِالجَمرَةِ الكُبرى لَهُ ثَمَّ أَوحَشَت — دِيارٌ وَعَرصاتٌ وَرَبعٌ وَمَولِدُ
units.en: And at the Great Jamrah, and at his ancient homes, open spaces, dwelling places, and birthplace, all grew lonely.

units.ar: فَبَكّي رَسولَ اللَهِ يا عَينُ عَبرَةً — وَلا أَعرِفَنكِ الدَهرَ دَمعَكِ يَجمَدُ
units.en: Then weep for the Messenger of Allah, O eye, with a flood of tears, and let me never find your tears running dry!

units.ar: وَما لَكِ لا تَبكينَ ذا النِعمَةِ الَّتي — عَلى الناسِ مِنها سابِغٌ يَتَغَمَّدُ
units.en: What ails you that you weep not for the possessor of bounty from whom a generous abundance covered all mankind?

units.ar: فَجودي عَلَيهِ بِالدُموعِ وَأَعوِلي — لِفَقدِ الَذي لا مِثلُهُ الدَهرُ يوجَدُ
units.en: Be generous then upon him with tears and wail aloud for the loss of him whose like time shall never produce!

units.ar: وَما فَقَدَ الماضونَ مِثلَ مُحَمَّدٍ — وَلا مِثلُهُ حَتّى القِيامَةِ يُفقَدُ
units.en: The ancients never lost the like of Muḥammad, nor shall his like ever be lost until the Day of Resurrection!

units.ar: أَعَفَّ وَأَوفى ذِمَّةً بَعدَ ذِمَّةٍ — وَأَقرَبَ مِنهُ نايِلاً لا يُنَكَّدُ
units.en: Most chaste, most faithful to covenants time after time, and closest to granting benefaction that is never spoiled,

units.ar: وَأَبذَلَ مِنهُ لِلطَريفِ وَتالِدِ — إِذا ضَنَّ مِعطاءُ بِما كانَ يُتلَدُ
units.en: Most generous of all in giving of newly acquired and inherited wealth, when any other giver withheld what was possessed,

units.ar: وَأَكرَمَ صيتاً في البُيوتِ إِذا اِنتَمى — وَأَكرَمَ جَدّاً أَبطَحيّاً يُسَوَّدُ
units.en: Most honorable in reputation among noble houses when traced, and most noble of grandfathers among the lords of the valley,

units.ar: وَأَمنَعَ ذِرواتٍ وَأَثبَتَ في العُلى — دَعائِمَ عِزٍّ شامِخاتٍ تُشَيَّدُ
units.en: Most unassailable in peaks, and most firmly established in high nobility, raising lofty pillars of glory that endure,

units.ar: وَأَثبَتَ فَرعاً في الفُروعِ وَمَنبِتاً — وَعوداً غَذاهُ المُزنُ فَالعودُ أَغيَدُ
units.en: Firmest in branch among the branches and lineage, and a noble bough nourished by rainclouds, so the bough is lush and green.

units.ar: رَباهُ وَليداً فَاِستَتَمَّ تَمامُهُ — عَلى أَكرَمِ الخَيراتِ رَبٌّ مُمَجَّدُ
units.en: A Glorious Lord nurtured him as a child until his perfection was complete in the noblest of virtues.

units.ar: تَناهَت وَصاةُ المُسلِمينَ بِكَفِّهِ — فَلا العِلمِ مَحبوسٌ وَلا الرَأيُ يُفنَدُ
units.en: The guidance of the Muslims culminated in his hands, so knowledge is never restrained nor is sound judgment refuted.

units.ar: أَقولُ وَلا يُلفى لِما قُلتُ عائِبٌ — مِنَ الناسِ إِلّا عازِبُ العَقلِ مُبعَدُ
units.en: I speak, and none shall find fault with what I utter among mankind, save one absent of mind and outcast.

units.ar: وَلَيسَ هَوايَ نازِعاً عَن ثَنائِهِ — لَعَلّي بِهِ في جَنَّةِ الخُلدِ أَخلَدُ
units.en: Nor does my devotion ever turn away from praising him; perhaps through it I may dwell forever in the Garden of Eternity,

units.ar: مَعَ المُصطَفى أَرجو بِذاكَ جِوارَهُ — وَفي نَيلِ ذاكَ اليَومِ أَسعى وَأَجهَدُ
units.en: With the Chosen One ﷺ, hoping thereby for his neighborliness, and toward attaining that Day I strive with all my might!

sections.heading: The Oath
sections.note: A sworn elegy — that no woman ever bore his like: poem 134 of the dīwān, also transmitted in Ibn Hishām’s Sīra; its fifth verse survives only in the dīwān.

units.ar: آلَيْتُ حَلْفَةَ بَرٍّ غَيْرَ ذِي دَخْلٍ — مِنِّي آلِيَّةُ بَرٍّ غَيْرِ إِفْنَادِ
units.en: I have sworn an oath of piety free of defect — an oath of piety from me, free of falsehood:

units.ar: بِاللهِ مَا حَمَلَتْ أُنْثَى وَلَا وَضَعَتْ — مِثْلَ النَّبِيِّ رَسُولِ الرَّحْمَةِ الْهَادِي
units.en: By Allah, no woman has ever carried or borne the like of the Prophet, the messenger of mercy, the guide,

units.ar: وَلَا مَشَى فَوْقَ ظَهْرِ الْأَرْضِ مِنْ أَحَدِ — أَوْفَى بِذِمَّةِ جَارٍ أَوْ بِمِيعَادِ
units.en: nor has anyone walked upon the face of the earth more true to a neighbour's protection or to a promise,

units.ar: مِنَ الَّذِي كَانَ نُورًا يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ — مُبَارَكُ الْأَمْرِ ذَا حَزْمٍ وَإِرْشَادِ
units.en: than the one who was a light by which light is sought, blessed in his affair, a man of resolve and right guidance,

units.ar: مُصَدِّقًا لِلتَّبِيِّنِ الْأُولَى تَلَقَّوْا — وَأَبْدَلَ النَّاسَ لِلْمَعْرُوفِ لِلْجَارِي
units.en: confirming what the first followers received; and he recompensed people with goodness for whoever sought it,

units.ar: خَيْرَ الْبَرِيَّةِ التَّقِيَّ كُنْتُ فِي نَهْرٍ — جَارٍ فَأَصْبَحْتُ مِثْلَ الْمُفْرَدِ الضَّادِي
units.en: the best of creation, the God-fearing. I was once in a flowing river; now I have become like a lone, thirsty man.

units.ar: أَمْسَى نِسَاؤُكَ عَطْلَى الْبُيُوتِ فَمَا — يَضْرِبْنَ فَوْقَ قَفَا سِتْرٍ بِأَوْتَادِ
units.en: Your womenfolk’s houses now stand empty: they pitch no curtained shelter with tent-pegs,

units.ar: مِثْلَ الرَّوَاهِبِ يَلْبَسْنَ الْمُسُوحَ فَقَدْ — أَيْقَنَّ بِالْبُوسِ بَعْدَ النِّعْمَةِ الْبَادِي
units.en: like nuns who have donned hair-cloth, certain now of ruin after the blessing that had been plain to see.

sections.heading: The Years in Makkah
sections.note: A retrospective on the Prophet’s ﷺ life, probably composed after his death — poem 19 of the dīwān, ending with the confession of faith in verse. Much of it is also ascribed to Abū Qays ibn Ṣirma.

units.ar: نَوَى بِمَكَّةَ بِضْعَ عَشَرَةَ حِجَّةً — يُذَكِّرُ لَوْ يَلْقَى خَلِيلًا مُؤَاتِيًا
units.en: He dwelt in Makkah some thirteen years, ever reminding — hoping yet to meet a true friend who would take him in,

units.ar: وَيَعْرِضُ فِي أَهْلِ الْمَوَاسِمِ نَفْسَهُ — فَلَمْ يَرَ مَنْ يُؤَاوِي وَلَمْ يَرَ دَاعِيَا
units.en: and he would offer himself to the people of the pilgrimage seasons, yet saw none who would shelter him, and saw no caller.

units.ar: فَلَمَّا أَتَانَا وَأَطْمَأَنَّتْ بِهِ النَّوَى — فَأَضْبَحَ مَسْرُورًا بِطَيْبَةَ رَاضِيَا
units.en: Then when he came to us and the people settled at rest with him, he awoke joyful in Ṭaybah, well-pleased,

units.ar: وَأَصْبَحَ لَا يَخْشَى عَدَاوَةَ ظَالِمٍ — قَرِيبٍ وَلَا يَخْشَى مِنَ النَّاسِ بَاغِيَا
units.en: and he came to fear no oppressor’s enmity near at hand, nor any aggressor among the people.

units.ar: بَذَلْنَا لَهُ الْأَمْوَالَ مِنْ مُحِلِّ مَالِنَا — وَأَنْفُسَنَا عِنْدَ الْوَغَى وَالْعَانِيَا
units.en: We spent for him our wealth from the lawful portion of our property, and our very selves in the battle’s heat and in hardship,

units.ar: نُحَارِبُ مَنْ عَادَى مِنَ النَّاسِ كُلِّهِمْ — جَمِيعًا وَإِنْ كَانَ الْحَبِيبُ الْمُصَافِيَا
units.en: fighting whoever shows enmity among all people, all together — even were he the dearest, most intimate friend.

units.ar: وَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا رَبَّ غَيْرُهُ — وَأَنَّ كِتَابَ اللهِ أَضْحَى هَادِيَا
units.en: And we know that Allah — there is no Lord but Him — and that the Book of Allah has become our guide.

works.author: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr
works.description_en: The celebrated ode with which Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr sought the Prophet's ﷺ forgiveness. When Kaʿb recited it before him in the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ pardoned him and cast his own mantle (burda) over his shoulders — the gift that gives this library its name. The Arabic text follows the recension transmitted in Ibn Hishām's Sīra; the English translation of the ode is J. W. Redhouse's (1881), in the public domain. Both are free of copyright.

sections.heading: The Qaṣīda

units.ar:
بَانَتْ سُعَادُ فَقَلْبِي الْيَوْمَ مُتَبْوِلُ
مُتَيَّمٌ إِثْرَهَا لَمْ يُفْدَ مَكْبُولُ
units.en: Su'ād hath departed. Therefore was my heart that day distracted, raving after her, irredeemably enchained.
units.en2: Suʿād has departed, and that day my heart was left reeling — lovesick, chasing after her, a captive no ransom can free.

units.ar:
وَمَا سُعَادُ غَدَاةَ الْبَيْنِ إِذْ رَحَلُوا
إِلَّا أَغَنُّ غَضِيضُ الطَّرْفِ مَكْحُولُ
units.en: On the morrow of our separation, when she went forth, Su'ād was no other than a bleating antelope, with downcast glance, and eyes set off with collyrium.
units.en2: On the morning of parting, when they broke camp, Suʿād was like a tender gazelle — soft-voiced, shy-eyed, her lashes dark with kohl.

units.ar:
هَيْفَاءُ مُقْبِلَةً عَجْزَاءُ مُدْبِرَةً
لَا يُشْتَكَى قِصَرٌ مِنْهَا وَلَا طُولُ
units.en: Slender of waist as she approaches, full-figured as she turns away — no shortness in her to complain of, and no excess of height.
units.en2: Slim of waist as she comes toward you, ample as she turns away — no shortness in her to complain of, and no excess of height.

units.ar:
تَجْلُو عَوَارِضَ ذِي ظَلْمٍ إِذَا ابْتَسَمَتْ
كَأَنَّهُ مُنْهَلٌ بِالرَّاحِ مَعْلُولُ
units.en: When she smiles, she displays [a row of] teeth of glancing whiteness, as though it had been a damaskeened sword-blade, once tempered, and then dipped a second time in wine,
units.en2: When she smiles, she shows teeth of dazzling whiteness, like a watered sword-blade, tempered once and then plunged a second time in wine —

units.ar:
شُجَّتْ بِذِي شَيَمٍ مِنْ مَاءِ مَحْنِيَةٍ
صَافٍ بِأَبْطَحَ أَضْحَى وَهْوَ مَشْمُولُ
units.en: Dashed, on a cold day, with water from a meandering stream, clear, and flowing in a wide, pebbly channel, fanned by a north wind when the day is high;
units.en2: splashed, on a cold day, with water from a winding stream, clear water running through a broad pebbly bed, fanned by the north wind at high noon,

units.ar:
تَنْفِي الرِّيَاحُ الْقَذَى عَنْهُ وَأَفْرَطَهُ
مِنْ صَوْبِ غَادِيَةٍ بَيْضُ يَعَالِيلُ
units.en: From which the winds banish all sticks and straws, and on which the silvery bubbles raised by a morning rain appear in great numbers.
units.en2: from which the winds sweep every twig and straw, and where the silvery bubbles of a morning rain gather in crowds.

units.ar:
قِيَالُهَا خُلَّةٌ لَوْ أَنَّهَا صَدَقَتْ
بِوَعْدِهَا أَوْ لَوْ أَنَّ النَّصْحَ مَقْبُولُ
units.en: God bless her mother! for the darling she would have been, had she kept true to her promise, and if advice had been acceptable [to her]!
units.en2: God bless her mother — what a darling she would have been, had she only kept her promise, and had good advice ever been taken!

units.ar:
لَكِنَّهَا خُلَّةٌ قَدْ سِيطَ مِنْ دَمِهَا
فَجْعٌ وَوَلْعٌ وَإِخْلَافٌ وَتَبْدِيلُ
units.en: But she is a darling, in the very blood of whom are blended pain, anxiety, disappointment, and change!
units.en2: But she is a darling in whose very blood are blended hurt, restless longing, broken promises, and fickleness.

units.ar:
فَمَا تَدُومُ عَلَى حَالٍ تَكُونُ بِهَا
كَمَا تَلَوَّنُ فِي أَثْوَابِهَا الْغُولُ
units.en: She remains not constant to any state she may have assumed, even as the demon of the wilds varies in its costume!
units.en2: She never stays constant in any state she takes, just as the desert demon keeps changing its costume.

units.ar:
وَمَا تَمَسَّكُ بِالْعَهْدِ الَّذِي زَعَمَتْ
إِلَّا كَمَا يُمْسِكُ الْمَاءَ الْغَرَابِيلُ
units.en: She does not hold to any promise she has spoken, save as sieves hold water!
units.en2: She holds to no promise she has made — she holds it the way sieves hold water.

units.ar:
فَلَا يَغُرَّنْكَ مَا مَنَّتْ وَمَا وَعَدَتْ
إِنَّ الْأَمَانِيَّ وَالْأَحْلَامَ تَضْلِيلُ
units.en: Let not, then, that deceive thee which she has bestowed, or which she has promised. Verily, desires and dreams are a delusion!
units.en2: So do not be deceived by what she grants or what she promises; wishes and dreams are nothing but delusion.

units.ar:
كَانَتْ مَوَاعِيدُ عُرْقُوبٍ لَهَا مَثَلًا
وَمَا مَوَاعِيدُهَا إِلَّا الْأَبَاطِيلُ
units.en: [The proverbial expression,] "the promises of ’Urqūb" is [as it were] a parable concerning her; and his promises were naught but lies!
units.en2: "The promises of ʿUrqūb" might have been coined as a parable about her — and his promises were nothing but lies.

units.ar:
أَرْجُو وَآمُلُ أَنْ تَدْنُو مَوَدَّتُهَا
وَمَا إِخَالُ لَدَيْنَا مِنْكِ تَنْوِيلُ
units.en: I wish and desire that they would become present in an eternity: but what ails them, then? I feel the whole duration of time an impatience!
units.en2: I long and hope that her affection might draw near — but I do not think you will ever grant us that.

units.ar:
أَمْسَتْ سُعَادُ بِأَرْضٍ لَا يُبَلِّغُهَا
إِلَّا الْعِتَاقُ النَّجِيبَاتُ الْمَرَاسِيلُ
units.en: Su'ād is to-day in a land where naught can enable one to reach her, save the noble, generous, free-going she-camels.
units.en2: Suʿād now dwells in a land that nothing can reach but noble, thoroughbred, free-running camels.

units.ar:
وَلَنْ يُبَلِّغَهَا إِلَّا عُذَافِرَةٌ
لَهَا عَلَى الْأَيْنِ إِرْقَالٌ وَتَبْغِيلُ
units.en: And certainly nothing could carry one to her, save a huge and dauntless she-camel, possessed, against fatigue, of speed and endurance;
units.en2: And nothing could carry one to her but a mighty, dauntless she-camel, armed against weariness with speed and staying power —

units.ar:
مِنْ كُلِّ نَضَّاخَةِ الذِّفْرَى إِذَا عَرِقَتْ
عُرْضَتُهَا طَامِسُ الْأَعْلَامِ مَجْهُولُ
units.en: Of those which drench the roots of their ears when they sweat; whose unknown energy blurs all the road-marks;
units.en2: one of those that soak the roots of their ears when they sweat, whose untried strength blots out the road-marks,

units.ar:
تَرْمِي الْغُيُوبَ بِعَيْنَيْ مُفْرِدٍ لَهِقٍ
إِذَا تَوَقَّدَتِ الْحِزَّانُ وَالْمِيلُ
units.en: Who looks at the highlands with the eyes of an isolated white addax, when the rocky flats and sand-hills are [as it were] on fire;
units.en2: who scans the uplands with the eyes of a lone white oryx, when the rocky flats and the sand-hills are ablaze with heat;

units.ar:
ضَخْمٌ مُقَلَّدُهَا فَعْمٌ مُقَيَّدُهَا
فِي خَلْقِهَا عَنْ بَنَاتِ الْفَحْلِ تَفْضِيلُ
units.en: Whose neck is thick where her collar sits; whose pastern is plump; in whose build there is a superiority over the daughters of the stallion-camel;
units.en2: thick of neck where the collar sits, plump of pastern — in build she outclasses the stallion-camel's daughters;

units.ar:
غَلْبَاءُ وَجْنَاءُ عُلْكُومٌ مُذَكَّرَةٌ
فِي دَفِّهَا سَعَةٌ قُدَّامُهَا مِيلُ
units.en: Large-headed, large-jawed, strongly formed; in whose side is capaciousness; whose neck is an obelisk;
units.en2: large-headed, wide-jawed, strongly made; roomy of flank, her neck like an obelisk;

units.ar:
وَجِلْدُهَا مِنْ أُطُومٍ مَا يُؤَيِّسُهُ
طِلْحٌ بِضَاحِيَةِ الْمَتْنَيْنِ مَهْزُولُ
units.en: Whose hide is that of a sea-turtle, on which tikes, slim in the loins and meagre, can make no impression;—
units.en2: her hide like a sea-turtle's shell, on which lean-bellied ticks lose all hope;

units.ar:
حَرْفٌ أَخُوهَا أَبُوهَا مِنْ مُهَجَّنَةٍ
وَعَمُّهَا خَالُهَا قَوْدَاءُ شِمْلِيلُ
units.en: A graceful creature; whose brother is her father out of a full-blooded dam, and whose paternal uncle is also her maternal uncle; who is long in the back, and agile;
units.en2: a graceful creature — her brother is her father by a full-blooded dam, her paternal uncle her maternal uncle too; long-backed and nimble;

units.ar:
يَمْشِي الْقُرَادُ عَلَيْهَا ثُمَّ يُزْلِقُهُ
مِنْهَا لَبَانٌ وَأَقْرَابٌ زَهَالِيلُ
units.en: Upon whom the tikes crawl; which are then dropped off by a chest and by flanks that are sleek;—
units.en2: ticks crawl over her, then slip away, shed by a chest and flanks too sleek to hold them;

units.ar:
عَيْرَانَةٌ قُذِفَتْ بِالنَّحْضِ عَنْ عُرُضٍ
مِرْفَقُهَا عَنْ بَنَاتِ الزَّوْرِ مَفْتُولُ
units.en: A very wild-ass; who, from plumpness, might be accused of too much flesh; whose elbow is twisted out from her chest-ribs;
units.en2: a very wild ass — so plump she might be accused of too much flesh, her elbow twisted clear of her chest-ribs,

units.ar:
كَأَنَّمَا فَاتَ عَيْنَيْهَا وَمَذْبَحَهَا
مِنْ خَطْمِهَا وَمِنَ اللَّحْيَيْنِ بِرْطِيلُ
units.en: As though what stands out in front of her two eyes and of the stabbing-place of her throat, as her muzzle and jaw-sides, were a millstone-pick;
units.en2: as if what juts before her eyes and her throat's stabbing-place — her muzzle and jaw-sides — were a millstone-pick;

units.ar:
تَمُرُّ مِثْلَ عَسِيبِ النَّخْلِ ذَا خُصَلٍ
فِي غَارِزٍ لَمْ تَخَوَّنْهُ الْأَحَالِيلُ
units.en: Who whisks [a tail] the like of a palm-branch, set with tufts of hair, against a flat udder, which the teats have never made to shrink;
units.en2: she swishes a tail like a tufted palm-frond against a firm udder that suckling has never shrunk;

units.ar:
قَنْوَاءُ فِي حُرَّتَيْهَا لِلْبَصِيرِ بِهَا
عِتْقٌ مُبِينٌ وَفِي الْخَدَّيْنِ تَسْهِيلُ
units.en: Aquiline of nose; in whose ears, to an observer, there is manifest nobility; in whose cheeks is a smoothness;
units.en2: aquiline of nose; in her ears, to anyone who can read a camel, plain nobility; smoothness in her cheeks;

units.ar:
تَخْدِي عَلَى يَسَرَاتٍ وَهْيَ لَاحِقَةٌ
ذَوَابِلٍ مَسُّهُنَّ الْأَرْضَ تَحْلِيلُ
units.en: Who, as she plays, alights on agile, slender legs, the fall of which on the earth is a mere pat;
units.en2: frisking along on slender, agile legs whose touch on the ground is a mere pat —

units.ar:
سُمْرُ الْعُجَايَاتِ يَتْرُكْنَ الْحَصَى زِيَمًا
لَمْ يَقِهِنَّ رُءُوسَ الْأُكَمِ تَنْعِيلُ
units.en: Dusky in their tendinous parts, which leave the pebbles scattered; and which no [leather] shoeing protects from the black [basaltic] stones of the hills,
units.en2: dusky at the tendons, they scatter the pebbles, and no leather shoeing guards them from the hills' black stones.

units.ar:
كَأَنَّ أَوْبَ ذِرَاعَيْهَا وَقَدْ عَرِقَتْ
وَقَدْ تَلَفَّعَ بِالْقُورِ الْعَسَاقِيلُ
units.en: The alternating play of whose fore-legs [they having already sweated, and the mirages having already shone on the rocks]
units.en2: The to-and-fro play of her forelegs — she sweating now, the mirage shimmering on the rocks —

units.ar:
يَوْمًا يَظَلُّ بِهِ الْحِرْبَاءُ مُصْطَخِدًا
كَأَنَّ ضَاحِيَهُ بِالشَّمْسِ مَمْلُولُ
units.en: On which, by day, the chameleon remains on the outlook, as though his back, exposed to the sun, were turned to ashes in the fire,
units.en2: on a day when the chameleon lies flattened on the lookout, its back, exposed to the sun, as if scorched to cinders,

units.ar:
وَقَالَ لِلْقَوْمِ حَادِيهِمْ وَقَدْ جَنَلَتْ
وُرْقُ الْجَنَادِبِ يَرْكُضْنَ الْحَصَا قِيلُوا
units.en: When the leader of a party has said to them—the piebald locusts having already begun to kick the pebbles—"Make your siesta;"
units.en2: when the riders' guide calls out to them — the speckled locusts already kicking at the pebbles — "Take your midday rest!" —

units.ar:
شَدَّ النَّهَارِ ذِرَاعَا عَيْطَلٍ نَصَفٍ
قَامَتْ فَجَاوَبَهَا نُكْدٌ مَثَاكِيلُ
units.en: Is [as it were] the alternating movement of the hands of a bereaved, grizzly, howling woman, standing up, and answered by [other] bereaved ones suffering from unsucked milk;
units.en2: is like the flailing arms of a bereaved, grey-haired, wailing woman who rises, answered by other mourners aching with unsuckled milk —

units.ar:
نَوَّاحَةٍ رِخْوَةِ الضَّبْعَيْنِ لَيْسَ لَهَا
لَمَّا نَعَى بِكْرَهَا النَّاعُونَ مَعْقُولُ
units.en: Lamenting, her arms drooping, deprived of reason when the bringers of bad news announced the [menaced] death of her first-born;
units.en2: keening, her arms gone slack, her reason fled since the bearers of ill tidings announced her firstborn's death —

units.ar:
تَفْرِي اللَّبَانَ بِكَفَّيْهَا وَمِدْرَعُهَا
مُشَقَّقٌ عَنْ تَرَاقِيهَا رَعَابِيلُ
units.en: Who tears her breast with her two hands, her corset being burst into tatters away from her chest-ribs;
units.en2: tearing at her breast with both hands, her bodice ripped to tatters from her collar-bones.

units.ar:
تَسْعَى الْغُوَاةُ جَنَابَيْهَا وَقَوْلُهُمْ
إِنَّكَ يَا بْنَ أَبِي سُلْمَى لَمَقْتُولُ
units.en: By whose side walk the misinformers, their words being: "O thou son of Abū Sulmà, verily thou art already slain!"
units.en2: At her side walk the rumour-mongers, and their words are: "Son of Abū Sulmā, you are as good as slain!"

units.ar:
وَقَالَ كُلُّ صَدِيقٍ كُنْتُ آمُلُهُ
لَا أُلْهِيَنَّكَ إِنِّي عَنْكَ مَشْغُولُ
units.en: And each faithful friend, from whom I had entertained hope [of protection from Muhammad's emissaries], said to me: "I will not deceive thee; I am busy with other things than thee."
units.en2: And every trusted friend I had hoped in said to me: "I will not lie to you — I have other concerns than you."

units.ar:
فَقُلْتُ خَلُّوا سَبِيلِي لَا أَبَا لَكُمْ
فَكُلُّ مَا قَدَّرَ الرَّحْمَنُ مَفْعُولُ
units.en: Then I spoke out: "Make ye way for me;—may your fathers perish! For all that the Most Merciful [God] hath forewilled will be accomplished:
units.en2: So I said: "Clear my road — perdition take your fathers! Whatever the Most Merciful has decreed will come to pass:

units.ar:
كُلُّ ابْنِ أُنْثَى وَإِنْ طَالَتْ سَلَامَتُهُ
يَوْمًا عَلَى آلَةٍ حَدْبَاءَ مَحْمُولُ
units.en: "Every son of a female, long though his safety may be, is one day borne upon a ridged implement [a bier with a ridged lid]."
units.en2: every child of woman, however long his safety lasts, is carried one day on a hump-backed bier."

units.ar:
نُبِّئْتُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَوْعَدَنِي
وَالْعَفْوُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ مَأْمُولُ
units.en: I have been informed that the Apostle of God hath threatened me; but pardon is hoped for from the Apostle of God.
units.en2: Word has reached me that the Messenger of God has threatened me — yet pardon from the Messenger of God is a thing to be hoped for.

units.ar:
مَهْلًا هَدَاكَ الَّذِي أَعْطَاكَ نَافِلَةَ
الْقُرْآنِ فِيهَا مَوَاعِظٌ وَتَفْصِيلُ
units.en: "Respite!—May He guide thee [O Apostle!] aright, who hath given thee the free gift of the Qur’ān, in which are exhortations and detail!—
units.en2: "A little respite! May He guide you aright who gave you the free gift of the Qur'an, with its counsels and clear expositions!

units.ar:
لَا تَأْخُذَنِّي بِأَقْوَالِ الْوُشَاةِ وَلَمْ
أُذْنِبْ وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ فِيَّ الْأَقَاوِيلُ
units.en: "Punish me not, then, at the words of calumniators: for I have not offended, though stories have multiplied concerning me."
units.en2: Do not punish me for the words of slanderers; I have done no wrong, however many tales about me multiply."

units.ar:
لَقَدْ أَقُومُ مَقَامًا لَوْ يَقُومُ بِهِ
أَرَى وَأَسْمَعُ مَا لَوْ يَسْمَعُ الْفِيلُ
units.en: Verily, I occupy a position, such that, were the elephant [of Abraha] to occupy it, and were to see and hear what I hear [and see],
units.en2: I stand in a station where, if Abraha's elephant stood — seeing and hearing what I see and hear —

units.ar:
لَظَلَّ يَرْعَدُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ
مِنَ الرَّسُولِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ تَنْوِيلُ
units.en: Out of distraction would his shoulders tremble, unless generosity were shown by the Apostle of God.
units.en2: its shoulders would quake with terror, unless the Messenger of God, by God's leave, showed it mercy.

units.ar:
حَتَّى وَضَعْتُ يَمِينِي مَا أُنَازِعُهُ
فِي كَفِّ ذِي نَقِمَاتٍ قِيلُهُ الْقِيلُ
units.en: Until I have placed my right hand, which I will not remove, in the palm of him who had a claim to vengeance,—whose word is the word.
units.en2: Until I laid my right hand — never to withdraw it — in the palm of one who had a claim to vengeance, whose word is the word.

units.ar:
فَلَهُوَ أَخْوَفُ عِنْدِي إِذْ أُكَلِّمُهُ
وَقِيلَ إِنَّكَ مَنْسُوبٌ وَمَسْئُولُ
units.en: A mere plaything unto me was the most terrible object, when I spoke to him, and it was said [unto me]: "Thou art accused and responsible!"
units.en2: The most terrifying thing on earth was a mere plaything to me when I spoke with him, and it was said: "You stand accused, and answerable!"

units.ar:
مِنْ ضَيْغَمٍ بِضَرَاءِ الْأَرْضِ مُخْدَرُهُ
فِي بَطْنِ عَثَّرَ غِيلٌ دُونَهُ غِيلُ
units.en: By a lion, whose den is in a level spot of the land, in the marshy hollow of ‘Aththar, surrounded by jungle upon jungle;
units.en2: By a lion whose lair lies on a level stretch of land, in the marshy hollow of ʿAththar, thicket beyond thicket,

units.ar:
يَغْدُو فَيُلْحِمُ ضِرْغَامَيْنِ عَيْشُهُمَا
لَحْمُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَعْفُورٌ خَرَادِيلُ
units.en: Who goes forth in the morning and provides with food two cubs, that feed on the flesh of men soiled in the dust and torn into fragments;
units.en2: who sets out at dawn and feeds two cubs whose diet is the flesh of men, soiled with dust and torn to pieces;

units.ar:
إِذَا يُسَاوِرُ قِرْنًا لَا يَحِلُّ لَهُ
أَنْ يَتْرُكَ الْقِرْنَ إِلَّا وَهُوَ مَفْلُولُ
units.en: Who, when he attacks his equal, is not permitted to leave that equal otherwise than mortified;
units.en2: when he closes with his match, he cannot leave that match except humbled and broken;

units.ar:
مِنْهُ تَظَلُّ سِبَاعُ الْجَوِّ نَافِرَةً
وَلَا تَمَشَّى بِوَادِيهِ الْأَرَاجِيلُ
units.en: From whom the wild asses of the desert take flight, and in whose valley bands of men cannot march;
units.en2: from him the wild asses of the waste flee in fright, and no band of men may march through his valley;

units.ar:
وَلَا يَزَالُ بِوَادِيهِ أَخُو ثِقَةٍ
مُضَرَّجُ الْبَزِّ وَالدُّرْسَانِ مَأْكُولُ
units.en: In whose valley there never lacks a man of courage, whose weapons are soiled with blood, his garments in shreds, and [himself] eaten!
units.en2: and in his valley there is never wanting a fearless man, his mail soaked with blood, his garments in shreds — and himself devoured!

units.ar:
إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَنُورٌ يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ
مُهَنَّدٌ مِنْ سُيُوفِ اللَّهِ مَسْلُولُ
units.en: Verily the Apostle of God is a Light from which illumination is sought: a drawn Indian blade—one of the Swords of God;
units.en2: Truly the Messenger is a light from which light is taken — a keen Indian blade, one of the drawn swords of God,

units.ar:
فِي عُصْبَةٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ قَالَ قَائِلُهُمْ
بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ لَمَّا أَسْلَمُوا زُولُوا
units.en: Among a small band of the Quraysh, whose spokesman said, in the Vale of Makka, when they had embraced Islām: "Depart ye!"
units.en2: among a company of Quraysh whose spokesman said, in the valley of Mecca, when they embraced Islam: "Depart!"

units.ar:
زَالُوا فَمَا زَالَ أَنْكَاسٌ وَلَا كُشُفٌ
عِنْدَ اللِّقَاءِ وَلَا مِيلٌ مَعَازِيلُ
units.en: And they did depart. But there departed not [among them] the poltroons, the dastards in time of the encounter, the puny, and the unarmed.
units.en2: And they departed — but no faint hearts departed with them, no cowards at the clash of battle, no weaklings, none unarmed.

units.ar:
شُمُّ الْعَرَانِينِ أَبْطَالٌ لَبُوسُهُمْ
مِنْ نَسْجِ دَاوُدَ فِي الْهَيْجَا سَرَابِيلُ
units.en: Aquiline-nosed heroes; whose clothing, in combat, is of shirts of the tissue of David—
units.en2: High-nosed champions whose battle-dress is shirts of David's weave —

units.ar:
بِيضٌ سَوَابِغُ قَدْ شُكَّتْ لَهَا حَلَقٌ
كَأَنَّهَا حَلَقُ الْقَفْعَاءِ مَجْدُولُ
units.en: Bright and ample, interlaced with links like the tendrils of the Qaf‘a plant, firmly wove together;
units.en2: white, ample coats of mail, their rings interlaced like the woven tendrils of the qafʿā plant;

units.ar:
لَيْسُوا مَفَارِيحَ إِنْ نَالَتْ رِمَاحُهُمْ
قَوْمًا وَلَيْسُوا مَجَازِيعَ إِذَا نِيلُوا
units.en: Who are not boisterously joyful if their lances wound a foe; and who piteously bewail not when wounded;
units.en2: they do not exult when their spears wound a people, nor do they wail in despair when they are wounded;

units.ar:
يَمْشُونَ مَشْيَ الْجِمَالِ الزُّهْرِ يَعْصِمُهُمْ
ضَرْبٌ إِذَا عَرَّدَ السُّودُ التَّنَابِيلُ
units.en: They walk with the gait of light-coloured camels;—a blow protects them; while the dwarfish tawny men [of Madīna] run away:
units.en2: they walk with the gait of white camels, protected by their striking when the dark-skinned weaklings slink away;

units.ar:
لَا يَقَعُ الطَّعْنُ إِلَّا فِي نُحُورِهِمْ
وَمَا لَهُمْ عَنْ حِيَاضِ الْمَوْتِ تَهْلِيلُ
units.en: Whom the spear-thrusts hit not, save on the front of their throats: for whom there is no shrinking back from the [battle-] pools of death!
units.en2: spear-thrusts strike them nowhere but the front of their throats, and they never shrink back from the death-pools of battle.

sections.note: Fifty-eight verses, as transmitted in Ibn Hishām's Sīra: the familiar opening to Suʿād, the camel that carried him, and the plea and praise recited before the Prophet ﷺ. English translation by J. W. Redhouse (1881); verse 3, not included in his edition, is rendered by this project.

sections.heading: The Verses of the Anṣār

units.ar:
مَنْ سَرَّهُ كَرْمُ الْحَيَاةِ فَلَا يَزَلْ
فِي مِقْنَبٍ مِنْ صَالِحِي الْأَنْصَارِ
units.en: Whoever delights in a life of honour, let him stay among a squadron of the righteous Helpers,

units.ar:
وَرِثُوا الْمَكَارِمَ كَابِرًا عَنْ كَابِرٍ
إِنَّ الْخِيَارَ هُمْ بَنُو الْأَخْيَارِ
units.en: who inherited noble ways, elder from elder — the best are ever the sons of the best.

units.ar:
الْمُكْرِهِينَ السَّمْهَرِيَّ بِأَذْرُعٍ
كَسَوَالِفِ الْهِنْدِيِّ غَيْرِ قِصَارِ
units.en: Who drive home the Samharī spear with arms like the long edges of Indian blades — nothing short about them,

units.ar:
وَالنَّاظِرِينَ بِأَعْيُنٍ مُحْمَرَّةٍ
كَالْجَمْرِ غَيْرُ كَلَيْلَةِ الْأَبْصَارِ
units.en: who glare with reddened eyes like embers, their gaze never wearying,

units.ar:
وَالْبَائِعِينَ نُفُوسَهُمْ لِنَبِيِّهِمْ
لِلْمَوْتِ يَوْمَ تَعَانُقٍ وَكِرَارِ
units.en: who sell their souls to their Prophet unto death, on the day of grappling and charge,

units.ar:
وَالْقَائِدِينَ النَّاسَ عَنْ أَدْيَانِهِمْ
بِالْمَشْرَفِيِّ وَبِالْقَنَا الْخَطَّارِ
units.en: who drive men away from their false religions with the Indian sword and the quivering spear.

units.ar:
يَتَطَهَّرُونَ يَرَوْنَهُ نُسْكًا لَهُمْ
بِدِمَاءِ مَنْ عَلِقُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ
units.en: They hold it an act of devotion to cleanse themselves in the blood of whichever unbelievers they catch.

units.ar:
دَرِبُوا كَمَا دَرِبَتْ بِبَطْنِ خُفَيَّةٍ
غُلْبُ الرِّقَابِ مِنَ الْأُسُودِ ضَوَارِي
units.en: They are battle-hardened as the thick-necked lions that prowl the vale of Khufayya are hardened to the hunt.

units.ar:
وَإِذَا حَلَلْتَ لِيَمْنَعُوكَ إِلَيْهِمْ
أَصْبَحْتَ عِنْدَ مَعَاقِلِ الْأَعْفَارِ
units.en: And if you camped against them, they would keep you off — you would wake amid the strongholds of ibex kids.

units.ar:
ضَرَبُوا عَلِيًّا يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ ضَرْبَةً
دَانَتْ لِوَقْعَتِهَا جَمِيعُ نِزَارِ
units.en: They struck the clan of ʿAliyy on the day of Badr a blow to which all of Nizār submitted.

units.ar:
لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الْأَقْوَامُ عِلْمِي كُلَّهُ
فِيهِمْ لَصَدَّقَنِي الَّذِينَ أُمَارِي
units.en: If the peoples knew all that I know of them, even those I dispute with would surely believe me.

units.ar:
قَوْمٌ إِذَا خَوَتِ النُّجُومُ فَإِنَّهُمْ
لِلطَّارِقِينَ النَّازِلِينَ مَقَارِي
units.en: A people who, when the stars set without bringing rain, are still a spread feast for guests who come by night,

units.ar:
فِي الْغُرِّ مِنْ غَسَّانَ مِنْ جُرْثُومَةٍ
أَعْيَتْ مَحَافِرُهَا عَلَى الْمِنْقَارِ
units.en: among the noblest of Ghassān, of a stock whose dug wells baffle the beak.

sections.note: After reciting the ode, Kaʿb was told the Prophet ﷺ wished he had praised the Anṣār too — so he added these verses in their honour. Redhouse did not translate these verses; the English is an original rendering for this project.

works.source_en: Arabic text follows the recension transmitted in Ibn Hishām's Sīra. The English translation of the ode is by J. W. Redhouse, from W. A. Clouston (ed.), Arabian Poetry for English Readers (Glasgow, 1881), pp. 305–318, now in the public domain. It is reproduced essentially verbatim, with two small exceptions: Redhouse's rendering of the beloved's name as “Beatrice” has been restored to Suʿād, and his verse 43 — a line found in his edition but absent from this recension — is omitted; verse 3 of the Arabic, which his edition did not include, keeps an original rendering made for this project. The Verses of the Anṣār were not translated by Redhouse and likewise keep their original rendering. A modern simplification in present-day English, made for this project, appears beneath the Victorian text on each verse as a reading aid. It is a simplification of the Victorian translation it accompanies, not a new translation of the Arabic. The Redhouse translation remains the citable text.

works.title_en: The Poem of the Mantle (Qaṣīdat al-Burdah)
works.author: al-Būṣīrī
works.description_en: The most celebrated poem in praise of the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ ever composed in Arabic. Sharaf al-Dīn al-Būṣīrī of Egypt wrote it after being stricken with paralysis; in a dream the Prophet ﷺ cast his own mantle (burdah) over the poet, and he awoke cured. Formally titled al-Kawākib al-Durriyya fī Madḥ Khayr al-Bariyya (“The Celestial Lights in Praise of the Best of Creation”), it runs to 161 verses in the basīṭ metre with a mīm rhyme, arranged in ten chapters — from the poet’s lovesick longing, through the Prophet’s birth, miracles and night journey, to the closing supplication. It is recited and sung across the Muslim world to this day.
works.source_en: Arabic: the received printed text of the Burdah, fully voweled, in the 161-verse recension that includes the verse “and upon the Family and the Companions, then their Successors” (v. 160). The seven supplementary verses and the refrain “Mawlāya ṣalli …” found in some modern prints are later additions not by al-Būṣīrī and are omitted. English: J. W. Redhouse’s complete translation, first published in W. A. Clouston (ed.), Arabian Poetry for English Readers (Glasgow, 1881), pp. 319–344, a public-domain work; Redhouse’s Victorian diction and his own bracketed glosses are kept verbatim. A modern simplification in present-day English, made for this project, appears beneath the Victorian text on each verse as a reading aid. It is a simplification of the Victorian translation it accompanies, not a new translation of the Arabic. The Redhouse translation remains the citable text.

sections.heading: On Yearning and the Lament of Love
sections.note: Verses 1–12

units.ar: أَمِنْ تَذَكُّرِ جِيرَانٍ بِذِي سَلَمِ — مَزَجْتَ دَمْعًا جَرَى مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ بِدَمِ
units.en: Is it from a recollection of neighbours at Dhū-Salam that thou hast mixed with blood the tears flowing from an eyeball?
units.en2: Is it remembering the neighbours at Dhū Salam that made you mix blood with the tears flowing from your eyes?

units.ar: أَمْ هَبَّتِ الرِّيحُ مِنْ تِلْقَاءِ كَاظِمَةٍ — وَأَوْمَضَ الْبَرْقُ فِي الظَّلْمَاءِ مِنْ إِضَمِ
units.en: Or, has the wind blown from the direction of Kādzima, and has the lightning gleamed in the darkness from Itzam?
units.en2: Or was it the wind blowing from Kāẓima, and lightning flashing through the darkness from Iḍam?

units.ar: فَمَا لِعَيْنَيْكَ إِنْ قُلْتَ اكْفُفَا هَمَتَا — وَمَا لِقَلْبِكَ إِنْ قُلْتَ اسْتَفِقْ يَهِمِ
units.en: What ails thy two eyes? If thou sayest, 'Leave off,' they fill. And what ails thy heart? If thou sayest, 'Be tranquil,' it is perplexed.
units.en2: What is wrong with your eyes? Tell them to stop, and they stream. What is wrong with your heart? Tell it to be calm, and it is thrown into turmoil.

units.ar: أَيَحْسَبُ الصَّبُّ أَنَّ الْحُبَّ مُنْكَتِمٌ — مَا بَيْنَ مُنْسَجِمٍ مِنْهُ وَمُضْطَرِمِ
units.en: Does the deeply-entangled lover suppose that affection can be concealed, when it is being partly wept for, and partly suffered for?
units.en2: Does the lovesick one imagine that love can be hidden, while it is being wept over and suffered for?

units.ar: لَوْلَا الْهَوَى لَمْ تُرِقْ دَمْعًا عَلَى طَلَلٍ — وَلَا أَرِقْتَ لِذِكْرِ الْبَانِ وَالْعَلَمِ
units.en: Were it not for fondness, thou hadst not shed tears over projecting ruins, neither hadst thou remained sleepless with the memory of the moringa-tree and the long hill.
units.en2: Were it not for passion, you would not have wept over the ruins, nor stayed sleepless remembering the moringa tree and the highland.

units.ar: فَكَيْفَ تُنْكِرُ حُبًّا بَعْدَ مَا شَهِدَتْ — بِهِ عَلَيْكَ عُدُولُ الدَّمْعِ وَالسَّقَمِ
units.en: And how wilt thou deny love, when the truth-speaking witnesses, tears and wasting, have testified to it against thee,
units.en2: How can you deny love, when two truthful witnesses — your tears and your wasting away — have testified against you,

units.ar: وَأَثْبَتَ الْوَجْدُ خَطَّيْ عَبْرَةٍ وَضَنًى — مِثْلَ الْبَهَارِ عَلَى خَدَّيْكَ وَالْعَنَمِ
units.en: And ardour hath fixed upon thy cheeks the two lines of grief and woe, like unto the corn-marigold and the 'anam?
units.en2: and longing has traced on your cheeks two lines of grief, like the corn-marigold and the red anemone?

units.ar: نَعَمْ سَرَى طَيْفُ مَنْ أَهْوَى فَأَرَّقَنِي — وَالْحُبُّ يَعْتَرِضُ اللَّذَّاتِ بِالْأَلَمِ
units.en: Yea! The phantom of her I love passed before me, and made me sleepless. For love doth dash delights with pain.
units.en2: Yes — the image of my beloved came to me in the night and robbed me of sleep; love mixes its delights with pain.

units.ar: يَا لَائِمِي فِي الْهَوَى الْعُذْرِيِّ مَعْذِرَةً — مِنِّي إِلَيْكَ وَلَوْ أَنْصَفْتَ لَمْ تَلُمِ
units.en: O my chider for an excusable affection! [receive] an excuse from me to thee: and if thou wert just, thou wouldst not have reproached me.
units.en2: You who blame me for a love I may be excused for — here is my excuse: if you were fair, you would not have blamed me.

units.ar: عَدَتْكَ حَالِيَ لَا سِرِّي بِمُسْتَتِرٍ — عَنِ الْوُشَاةِ وَلَا دَائِي بِمُنْحَسِمِ
units.en: My condition hath become manifest unto thee; my secret is not concealed from the traducers; nor is my disease cut off.
units.en2: My state is plain for you to see; my secret is not hidden from my slanderers, and my sickness has no cure.

units.ar: مَحَّضْتَنِي النُّصْحَ لَكِنْ لَسْتُ أَسْمَعُهُ — إِنَّ الْمُحِبَّ عَنِ الْعُذَّالِ فِي صَمَمِ
units.en: Thou hast given unto me sincere advice; but I listen not thereto. Verily a lover is in a state of surdity to all blamers!
units.en2: You gave me sincere advice, but I do not listen; a lover is deaf to everyone who blames him.

units.ar: إِنِّي اتَّهَمْتُ نَصِيحَ الشَّيْبِ فِي عَذَلٍ — وَالشَّيْبُ أَبْعَدُ فِي نُصْحٍ عَنِ التُّهَمِ
units.en: In truth, I have suspected my sincere gray hairs of being among my blamers; but my gray hairs are very far from blamings in giving advice.
units.en2: I even suspected my own grey hairs of being among my blamers — yet grey hairs are far above blame when they give advice.

audio.title: Chapter 1: On Yearning and the Lament of Love

sections.heading: Warning Against the Desires of the Soul
sections.note: Verses 13–28

units.ar: فَإِنَّ أَمَّارَتِي بِالسُّوءِ مَا اتَّعَظَتْ — مِنْ جَهْلِهَا بِنَذِيرِ الشَّيْبِ وَالْهَرَمِ
units.en: For, indeed, the dominating spirit that commands me to do evil has not accepted admonition, through its ignorance, from the warning voice of gray hairs and decrepitude;
units.en2: For my lower self, which commands me to do evil, paid no heed — in its ignorance — to the warning voice of grey hairs and old age,

units.ar: وَلَا أَعَدَّتْ مِنَ الْفِعْلِ الْجَمِيلِ قِرَى — ضَيْفٍ أَلَمَّ بِرَأْسِي غَيْرَ مُحْتَشِمِ
units.en: Neither has it made ready, out of good actions, a feast for the guest that has settled tenaciously on my head unabashed.
units.en2: nor has it prepared, out of good deeds, a feast for the guest that has settled unashamed upon my head.

units.ar: لَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ أَنِّي مَا أُوَقِّرُهُ — كَتَمْتُ سِرًّا بَدَا لِي مِنْهُ بِالْكَتَمِ
units.en: Had I known that I should not treat it with respect, I would have concealed with woad a secret that became revealed to me.
units.en2: Had I known I would fail to honour it, I would have hidden with dye the secret that came to show on me.

units.ar: مَنْ لِي بِرَدِّ جِمَاحٍ مِنْ غَوَايَتِهَا — كَمَا يُرَدُّ جِمَاحُ الْخَيْلِ بِاللُّجُمِ
units.en: Who is for me in checking perversity in its erratic movements, as the perversity of horses is checked with bits?
units.en2: Who will help me restrain the waywardness of a self that strays, the way unruly horses are restrained with bridles?

units.ar: فَلَا تَرُمْ بِالْمَعَاصِي كَسْرَ شَهْوَتِهَا — إِنَّ الطَّعَامَ يُقَوِّي شَهْوَةَ النَّهِمِ
units.en: Propose not, therefore, to crush its inclination in its acts of rebellion; for food invigorates desire in the insatiate.
units.en2: Do not think to crush its appetite when it rebels — feeding only sharpens desire in the greedy.

units.ar: وَالنَّفْسُ كَالطِّفْلِ إِنْ تُهْمِلْهُ شَبَّ عَلَى — حُبِّ الرَّضَاعِ وَإِنْ تَفْطِمْهُ يَنْفَطِمِ
units.en: The Flesh is like a child: if thou leavest him alone, he grows up with a love for suckling; and if thou weanest him, he is weaned.
units.en2: The lower self is like a child: leave it, and it grows up loving to suckle; wean it, and it is weaned.

units.ar: فَاصْرِفْ هَوَاهَا وَحَاذِرْ أَنْ تُوَلِّيَهُ — إِنَّ الْهَوَى مَا تَوَلَّى يُصْمِ أَوْ يَصِمِ
units.en: Turn, then, away its desire; and take heed lest thou make it thy master: for whomsoever desire masters, it kills, or binds fast.
units.en2: Turn its appetite away, and never let it become your master — desire, when it masters a person, kills them or binds them fast.

units.ar: وَرَاعِهَا وَهْيَ فِي الْأَعْمَالِ سَائِمَةٌ — وَإِنْ هِيَ اسْتَحْلَتِ الْمَرْعَى فَلَا تُسِمِ
units.en: And watch thou over it, while it grazes in the [field of] actions. Then, if it find the pasturage sweet to its taste, leave it not to pasture.
units.en2: Watch it as it grazes in the field of deeds; if it finds the pasture sweet, do not leave it to graze.

units.ar: كَمْ حَسَّنَتْ لَذَّةً لِلْمَرْءِ قَاتِلَةً — مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَنَّ السُّمَّ فِي الدَّسَمِ
units.en: How often hath it made a lethal thing appear pleasant of taste unto a man, while he knew not that poison was in the gravy!
units.en2: How often it makes a deadly thing taste sweet to a man who does not know there is poison in the sauce!

units.ar: وَاخْشَ الدَّسَائِسَ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَمِنْ شِبَعٍ — فَرُبَّ مَخْمَصَةٍ شَرٌّ مِنَ التُّخَمِ
units.en: And beware of artifices devised by hunger and satiety. For many an emptiness of stomach is more detrimental than indigestion.
units.en2: Beware the tricks of hunger and of fullness alike — many an empty stomach does more harm than overeating.

units.ar: وَاسْتَفْرِغِ الدَّمْعَ مِنْ عَيْنٍ قَدِ امْتَلَأَتْ — مِنَ الْمَحَارِمِ وَالْزَمْ حِمْيَةَ النَّدَمِ
units.en: And dash out the tears from thine eye that has filled from [a desire for] forbidden things; and strictly observe the diet of penitence.
units.en2: Wipe the tears from an eye that has wept over forbidden things, and keep strictly to the discipline of repentance.

units.ar: وَخَالِفِ النَّفْسَ وَالشَّيْطَانَ وَاعْصِهِمَا — وَإِنْ هُمَا مَحَضَاكَ النُّصْحَ فَاتَّهِمِ
units.en: And withstand thou the Flesh and the Devil, and rebel against them. Even when they offer thee sincere advice, doubt it.
units.en2: Resist the lower self and Satan, and defy them both; even when they offer you sincere advice, distrust it.

units.ar: وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمَا خَصْمًا وَلَا حَكَمًا — فَأَنْتَ تَعْرِفُ كَيْدَ الْخَصْمِ وَالْحَكَمِ
units.en: And be not thou obedient to them, either as adversary or arbiter; for thou art aware of the devices of the adversary and of the arbiter.
units.en2: Do not obey them, whether they come as opponent or as judge — you already know the tricks of the opponent and the judge.

units.ar: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ مِنْ قَوْلٍ بِلَا عَمَلٍ — لَقَدْ نَسَبْتُ بِهِ نَسْلًا لِذِي عُقُمِ
units.en: I ask forgiveness of God for my spoken words unaccompanied by deeds; for therewith have I accused a spouse of barren wives of having posterity.
units.en2: I ask God's forgiveness for words not matched by deeds — with them I credited a man of childless stock with offspring.

units.ar: أَمَرْتُكَ الْخَيْرَ لَكِنْ مَا ائْتَمَرْتُ بِهِ — وَمَا اسْتَقَمْتُ فَمَا قَوْلِي لَكَ اسْتَقِمِ
units.en: I have commanded thee [to do] good; but I have not [myself] conformed thereto. I have not been upright;—what, then, is my word to thee: Be upright?
units.en2: I told you to do good but did not do it myself; I was not upright — so what right have I to say to you: be upright?

units.ar: وَلَا تَزَوَّدْتُ قَبْلَ الْمَوْتِ نَافِلَةً — وَلَمْ أُصَلِّ سِوَى فَرْضٍ وَلَمْ أَصُمِ
units.en: I have not provisioned myself, before death, with a [store of] supererogatory good works; I have not worshipped, save as is incumbent; nor have I fasted [otherwise].
units.en2: Before death I laid up no store of voluntary good works; I never prayed beyond what is obligatory, nor fasted beyond it.

audio.title: Chapter 2: Warning Against the Desires of the Soul

sections.heading: In Praise of the Prophet ﷺ
sections.note: Verses 29–58

units.ar: ظَلَمْتُ سُنَّةَ مَنْ أَحْيَا الظَّلَامَ إِلَى — أَنِ اشْتَكَتْ قَدَمَاهُ الضُّرَّ مِنْ وَرَمِ
units.en: I have swerved from the practice of him who made the darkness [of night] alive [with his devotions], until his two feet complained of injury from tumefaction;
units.en2: I strayed from the way of the one who made the night alive with worship until his feet complained of the swelling,

units.ar: وَشَدَّ مِنْ سَغَبٍ أَحْشَاءَهُ وَطَوَى — تَحْتَ الْحِجَارَةِ كَشْحًا مُتْرَفَ الْأَدَمِ
units.en: And bound up his entrails from hunger, and girded beneath stones a tender-skinned hypochondriac region;
units.en2: who bound his stomach against hunger and wrapped stones beneath a tender-skinned belly.

units.ar: وَرَاوَدَتْهُ الْجِبَالُ الشُّمُّ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ — عَنْ نَفْسِهِ فَأَرَاهَا أَيَّمَا شَمَمِ
units.en: Whom the towering mountains sought to entice from his self-possession by talking about gold; but to which he exhibited a surprising loftiness;
units.en2: The towering mountains tried to tempt him out of his resolve with offers of gold, and he showed them a marvellous disdain;

units.ar: وَأَكَّدَتْ زُهْدَهُ فِيهَا ضَرُورَتُهُ — إِنَّ الضَّرُورَةَ لَا تَعْدُو عَلَى الْعِصَمِ
units.en: Whose necessity confirmed his disinclination towards them; for, verily, necessity doth not invade continences.
units.en2: his need only strengthened his refusal — for need can never storm a fortress of self-restraint.

units.ar: وَكَيْفَ تَدْعُو إِلَى الدُّنْيَا ضَرُورَةُ مَنْ — لَوْلَاهُ لَمْ تُخْرَجِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ الْعَدَمِ
units.en: Then, how could his necessity invite to [the things of] the world, him, without whom the world would not have come forth from naught?—
units.en2: And how could need have drawn him to this world, when without him the world would never have been brought out of nothingness?

units.ar: مُحَمَّدٌ سَيِّدُ الْكَوْنَيْنِ وَالثَّقَلَيْنِ — وَالْفَرِيقَيْنِ مِنْ عُرْبٍ وَمِنْ عَجَمِ
units.en: Muhammad, the Prince of the two universes [material and spiritual], of the two ponderable classes [men and demons], and of the two sections [of mankind], of the Arabians and of the Non-Arabians;
units.en2: Muḥammad — master of both worlds, of both burdened races, jinn and men, and of both branches of mankind, Arab and non-Arab;

units.ar: نَبِيُّنَا الْآمِرُ النَّاهِي فَلَا أَحَدٌ — أَبَرَّ فِي قَوْلِ لَا مِنْهُ وَلَا نَعَمِ
units.en: Our Annunciator, who commands and who prohibits; than whom no one is more righteous in the word "No!" or in [the word] "Yea!"
units.en2: our truthful messenger, who commands and forbids; none is truer than he in saying "no" or "yes";

units.ar: هُوَ الْحَبِيبُ الَّذِي تُرْجَى شَفَاعَتُهُ — لِكُلِّ هَوْلٍ مِنَ الْأَهْوَالِ مُقْتَحَمِ
units.en: Who is also the "Beloved One [of God];" whose intercession is hoped for in every terror, of the terrors that beset;
units.en2: the Beloved of God, whose intercession is hoped for in every terror that befalls;

units.ar: دَعَا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَالْمُسْتَمْسِكُونَ بِهِ — مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ بِحَبْلٍ غَيْرِ مُنْفَصِمِ
units.en: Who called [men and demons] to [obedience to] God; so that they who lay hold on him have hold of a cable that will not break;
units.en2: who called people to God — whoever holds fast to him has grasped a rope that never breaks;

units.ar: فَاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ فِي خَلْقٍ وَفِي خُلُقٍ — وَلَمْ يُدَانُوهُ فِي عِلْمٍ وَلَا كَرَمِ
units.en: Who surpassed [all] the prophets in manly form and in moral qualities; whom they do not approach in knowledge or in generosity;
units.en2: who surpassed the prophets in form and character; none comes near him in knowledge or in generosity;

units.ar: وَكُلُّهُمْ مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ مُلْتَمِسٌ — غَرْفًا مِنَ الْبَحْرِ أَوْ رَشْفًا مِنَ الدِّيَمِ
units.en: All of them supplicate the "Apostle of God" for a handful of [his] sea [of knowledge], or for a sip of [his] steady rain [of exposition];
units.en2: all of them beg the Messenger of God for a handful from his ocean, or a sip from his steady rain;

units.ar: وَوَاقِفُونَ لَدَيْهِ عِنْدَ حَدِّهِمِ — مِنْ نُقْطَةِ الْعِلْمِ أَوْ مِنْ شَكْلَةِ الْحِكَمِ
units.en: Compared with whom, they, in their degree, are cognisant of a [mere] dot of the [divine] knowledge, or a [bare] suspicion of [God's] wisdoms;
units.en2: beside him, their share of the divine knowledge is a dot, and of His wisdoms a mere inkling;

units.ar: فَهْوَ الَّذِي تَمَّ مَعْنَاهُ وَصُورَتُهُ — ثُمَّ اصْطَفَاهُ حَبِيبًا بَارِئُ النَّسَمِ
units.en: Whose outward form and inner significance the Creator of the soul perfected, and whom He then selected [as His] "Beloved One;"
units.en2: the one whose outer form and inner meaning the Creator of the soul perfected, then chose as His beloved;

units.ar: مُنَزَّهٌ عَنْ شَرِيكٍ فِي مَحَاسِنِهِ — فَجَوْهَرُ الْحُسْنِ فِيهِ غَيْرُ مُنْقَسِمِ
units.en: Who is unassociated with any partner in his beauties; in whom the essence of loveliness is undivided.
units.en2: without partner in his beauty — the very essence of loveliness, undivided in him.

units.ar: دَعْ مَا ادَّعَتْهُ النَّصَارَى فِي نَبِيِّهِمِ — وَاحْكُمْ بِمَا شِئْتَ مَدْحًا فِيهِ وَاحْتَكِمِ
units.en: Put aside that which the Nazarenes have laid claim to for their prophet; pronounce what thou wilt in his praise, and decide;
units.en2: Set aside what the Christians claim for their prophet; then say what you will in his praise, and judge freely:

units.ar: وَانْسُبْ إِلَى ذَاتِهِ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ شَرَفٍ — وَانْسُبْ إِلَى قَدْرِهِ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ عِظَمِ
units.en: Attribute to his personality what thou wilt of nobility; and ascribe to his worth what thou wilt of vastness;
units.en2: attribute to his person whatever nobility you wish, and to his worth whatever greatness you wish —

units.ar: فَإِنَّ فَضْلَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ — حَدٌّ فَيُعْرِبَ عَنْهُ نَاطِقٌ بِفَمِ
units.en: For verily the superiority of the Apostle of God hath no limit, that a speaker can clearly enunciate with his mouth concerning it.
units.en2: for the excellence of the Messenger of God has no limit that a speaker's mouth could ever express.

units.ar: لَوْ نَاسَبَتْ قَدْرَهُ آيَاتُهُ عِظَمًا — أَحْيَا اسْمُهُ حِينَ يُدْعَى دَارِسَ الرِّمَمِ
units.en: If his miracles had equalled his worth, his [very] name, when called upon, would have brought back to life mouldering bones fallen to pieces.
units.en2: Had his miracles matched his rank, his very name, when invoked, would have raised crumbling, decayed bones back to life.

units.ar: لَمْ يَمْتَحِنَّا بِمَا تَعْيَا الْعُقُولُ بِهِ — حِرْصًا عَلَيْنَا فَلَمْ نَرْتَبْ وَلَمْ نَهِمِ
units.en: But, out of anxious solicitude towards us, he hath not tried us with anything at which men's reasons break down; we therefore doubt not, nor vainly surmise.
units.en2: But out of tender care for us, he did not test us with anything that would break our reason — so we do not doubt, nor guess in vain.

units.ar: أَعْيَا الْوَرَى فَهْمُ مَعْنَاهُ فَلَيْسَ يُرَى — فِي الْقُرْبِ وَالْبُعْدِ فِيهِ غَيْرُ مُنْفَحِمِ
units.en: The comprehension of his spiritual mystery outwearies the human race; thou wilt, therefore, not see, far or near, any not out of breath [thereat];—
units.en2: The grasp of his true reality exhausts humankind; look near or far, and you will find no one not left breathless by it —

units.ar: كَالشَّمْسِ تَظْهَرُ لِلْعَيْنَيْنِ مِنْ بُعُدٍ — صَغِيرَةً وَتُكِلُّ الطَّرْفَ مِنْ أَمَمِ
units.en: Even as the sun at a distance appears small to our eyes, but fatigues the sight with over-closeness.
units.en2: like the sun: small to the eye from afar, yet blinding when you draw too close.

units.ar: وَكَيْفَ يُدْرِكُ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَقِيقَتَهُ — قَوْمٌ نِيَامٌ تَسَلَّوْا عَنْهُ بِالْحُلُمِ
units.en: And how should a sleeping people comprehend his reality in this lower world? They console themselves with dreams in lieu thereof.
units.en2: How can a sleeping people in this lower world comprehend his reality? They make do with dreams of it.

units.ar: فَمَبْلَغُ الْعِلْمِ فِيهِ أَنَّهُ بَشَرٌ — وَأَنَّهُ خَيْرُ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ كُلِّهِمِ
units.en: The utmost scope of [their] knowledge concerning him [is], that he was a man, and that he is the best of God's creatures—of the whole of them.
units.en2: The furthest reach of their knowledge of him: that he was a man — and that he is the best of all God's creation.

units.ar: وَكُلُّ آيٍ أَتَى الرُّسُلُ الْكِرَامُ بِهَا — فَإِنَّمَا اتَّصَلَتْ مِنْ نُورِهِ بِهِمِ
units.en: And all the signs that the noble apostles wrought [in former days] pertained unto them merely through his glory.
units.en2: Every sign the noble messengers worked of old came to them only through his light.

units.ar: فَإِنَّهُ شَمْسُ فَضْلٍ هُمْ كَوَاكِبُهَا — يُظْهِرْنَ أَنْوَارَهَا لِلنَّاسِ فِي الظُّلَمِ
units.en: For verily he is the sun of superiority, of which they are the stars. They exhibit their lights to the people in the darknesses [but the sun is visible by day].
units.en2: For he is the sun of excellence, and they are its stars, showing their light to people in the dark.

units.ar: أَكْرِمْ بِخَلْقِ نَبِيٍّ زَانَهُ خُلُقٌ — بِالْحُسْنِ مُشْتَمِلٍ بِالْبِشْرِ مُتَّسِمِ
units.en: How noble was the manly form of the Prophet; whom moral qualities adorned; whom beauty enveloped; and whom beauty of features distinguished!
units.en2: How noble was the Prophet's form — character adorned him, beauty clothed him, and handsome features set him apart:

units.ar: كَالزَّهْرِ فِي تَرَفٍ وَالْبَدْرِ فِي شَرَفٍ — وَالْبَحْرِ فِي كَرَمٍ وَالدَّهْرِ فِي هِمَمِ
units.en: Like the flowers in softness, and the full moon in splendour, and the sea in liberality, and time in endeavours!
units.en2: like the blossom in softness, the full moon in splendour, the sea in generosity, and time itself in high resolve.

units.ar: كَأَنَّهُ وَهْوَ فَرْدٌ مِنْ جَلَالَتِهِ — فِي عَسْكَرٍ حِينَ تَلْقَاهُ وَفِي حَشَمِ
units.en: Through his majesty, when thou meetest him, in an army, or in a body of attendants, it is as though he were a solitary individual!—
units.en2: Such is his majesty that when you meet him, even amid an army or a crowd of followers, it is as if he stood alone —

units.ar: كَأَنَّمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ الْمَكْنُونُ فِي صَدَفٍ — مِنْ مَعْدِنَيْ مَنْطِقٍ مِنْهُ وَمُبْتَسَمِ
units.en: As though the pearl enclosed in the shell were [composed] of the two ores—speech from him, and smiling!
units.en2: as if he were the pearl inside the shell, made of two precious elements: his speech and his smile.

units.ar: لَا طِيبَ يَعْدِلُ تُرْبًا ضَمَّ أَعْظُمَهُ — طُوبَى لِمُنْتَشِقٍ مِنْهُ وَمُلْتَثِمِ
units.en: There is no perfume to equal the earth that has enclosed his bones;—blessed is he that sniffs therefrom, and he who kisses [it]!
units.en2: No fragrance equals the earth that holds his body — blessed is the one who breathes it in and kisses it!

audio.title: Chapter 3: In Praise of the Prophet ﷺ

sections.heading: On His Blessed Birth ﷺ
sections.note: Verses 59–71

units.ar: أَبَانَ مَوْلِدُهُ عَنْ طِيبِ عُنْصُرِهِ — يَا طِيبَ مُبْتَدَإٍ مِنْهُ وَمُخْتَتَمِ
units.en: His birth made manifest the sweet-smelling goodness of his substance. How fragrant was the commencement thereof, and the conclusion!
units.en2: His birth revealed the sweet goodness of his origin — how fragrant its beginning, and how fragrant its end.

units.ar: يَوْمٌ تَفَرَّسَ فِيهِ الْفُرْسُ أَنَّهُمُ — قَدْ أُنْذِرُوا بِحُلُولِ الْبُؤْسِ وَالنِّقَمِ
units.en: [It was] a day in which the Persians sagaciously opined that they were warned of the happening of evil and of vengeance;
units.en2: It was a day on which the Persians understood they had been warned of coming calamity and punishment:

units.ar: وَبَاتَ إِيوَانُ كِسْرَى وَهْوَ مُنْصَدِعٌ — كَشَمْلِ أَصْحَابِ كِسْرَى غَيْرَ مُلْتَئِمِ
units.en: And the pavilion of the Chosroes became, being fissured, like unto the courtiers of the Chosroes, irremediably disarrayed;
units.en2: the hall of the Chosroes was split apart, as shattered beyond repair as his own courtiers;

units.ar: وَالنَّارُ خَامِدَةُ الْأَنْفَاسِ مِنْ أَسَفٍ — عَلَيْهِ وَالنَّهْرُ سَاهِي الْعَيْنِ مِنْ سَدَمِ
units.en: And the [Sacred] Fire, through sorrowfulness thereat, became extinct in its respirations [of flame], and the river [of the Tigris] dry at fount, through choking;
units.en2: the sacred fire of Persia died down in grief, and the river went dry at its source, choked with sorrow;

units.ar: وَسَاءَ سَاوَةَ أَنْ غَاضَتْ بُحَيْرَتُهَا — وَرُدَّ وَارِدُهَا بِالْغَيْظِ حِينَ ظَمِي
units.en: And it afflicted [the town of] Sāwa that its lake should sink into the earth, and that the corner thereto for water should be angrily repelled when he thirsted;—
units.en2: it grieved Sāwa that her lake sank into the ground, and the thirsty who came to her waters turned away in anger.

units.ar: كَأَنَّ بِالنَّارِ مَا بِالْمَاءِ مِنْ بَلَلٍ — حُزْنًا وَبِالْمَاءِ مَا بِالنَّارِ مِنْ ضَرَمِ
units.en: As though in the Fire [there was], through sadness, the wetness that is in water; and in the water, the [heart-]burning that is in fire;—
units.en2: It was as if the fire, in its sadness, held water's wetness, and the water held fire's burning.

units.ar: وَالْجِنُّ تَهْتِفُ وَالْأَنْوَارُ سَاطِعَةٌ — وَالْحَقُّ يَظْهَرُ مِنْ مَعْنًى وَمِنْ كَلِمِ
units.en: Then the genii make their voices heard; and the meteors are flashing, and the truth becomes manifest in sense and in words;
units.en2: Then the jinn cried out, meteors flashed, and the truth shone forth — in signs and in words —

units.ar: عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا فَإِعْلَانُ الْبَشَائِرِ لَمْ — تُسْمَعْ وَبَارِقَةُ الْإِنْذَارِ لَمْ تُشَمِ
units.en: [But men] were blind and deaf; so the proclamation of the good news was not heard; nor were the flaming admonitions heeded;
units.en2: but people were blind and deaf: they did not hear the glad announcement, nor heed the flaming warnings,

units.ar: مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَخْبَرَ الْأَقْوَامَ كَاهِنُهُمْ — بِأَنَّ دِينَهُمُ الْمُعْوَجَّ لَمْ يَقُمِ
units.en: Although their soothsayers had informed the peoples that their crooked religions would not stand;
units.en2: though their soothsayers had told the nations that their crooked religions would not stand,

units.ar: وَبَعْدَ مَا عَايَنُوا فِي الْأُفْقِ مِنْ شُهُبٍ — مُنْقَضَّةٍ وَفْقَ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ صَنَمِ
units.en: And though they had seen in the horizon blazing stars fallen, in like manner with what [took place] on earth with idols;
units.en2: and though they had seen shooting stars fallen from the horizon, just as the idols on earth had fallen.

units.ar: حَتَّى غَدَا عَنْ طَرِيقِ الْوَحْيِ مُنْهَزِمٌ — مِنَ الشَّيَاطِينِ يَقْفُو إِثْرَ مُنْهَزِمِ
units.en: Until it happened, by means of revelation, that one discomfited individual of the demons followed the footmarks of [another] discomfited one;
units.en2: Until, driven back by the revelation, one routed devil followed in the tracks of another,

units.ar: كَأَنَّهُمْ هَرَبًا أَبْطَالُ أَبْرَهَةٍ — أَوْ عَسْكَرٌ بِالْحَصَى مِنْ رَاحَتَيْهِ رُمِي
units.en: As though they were, in [their] flight, the cowards of Abraha, or the army lapidated with pebbles from his [Muhammad's] two hands,
units.en2: as if they were, in flight, the cowards of Abraha's army, or the host pelted with pebbles from his own two hands —

units.ar: نَبْذًا بِهِ بَعْدَ تَسْبِيحٍ بِبَطْنِهِمَا — نَبْذَ الْمُسَبِّحِ مِنْ أَحْشَاءِ مُلْتَقِمِ
units.en: In a throw, after a recitation of doxology within their two palms; even as the casting forth of the doxologist [Jonah] from the entrails of the swallowing fish;
units.en2: thrown after he had glorified God within his palms, as Jonah the glorifier was cast out of the belly of the whale.

audio.title: Chapter 4: On His Blessed Birth ﷺ

sections.heading: On His Miracles ﷺ
sections.note: Verses 72–87

units.ar: جَاءَتْ لِدَعْوَتِهِ الْأَشْجَارُ سَاجِدَةً — تَمْشِي إِلَيْهِ عَلَى سَاقٍ بِلَا قَدَمِ
units.en: At his [Muhammad's] call the trees came prostrating themselves, walking towards him on legs [trunks] without feet;
units.en2: At his call the trees came bowing down to him, walking towards him on trunks without feet,

units.ar: كَأَنَّمَا سَطَرَتْ سَطْرًا لِمَا كَتَبَتْ — فُرُوعُهَا مِنْ بَدِيعِ الْخَطِّ بِاللَّقَمِ
units.en: As though they were tracing lines for what their branches wrote, of a beautiful handwriting, in the main track of the path:
units.en2: as if they were drawing ruled lines for the beautiful script their branches wrote along the middle of the road —

units.ar: مِثْلَ الْغَمَامَةِ أَنَّى سَارَ سَائِرَةً — تَقِيهِ حَرَّ وَطِيسٍ لِلْهَجِيرِ حَمِي
units.en: Like the cloud, which followed wherever he went, shielding him from the oven-like heat of noontide waxed sultry.
units.en2: and like the cloud that followed him wherever he went, shading him when the noon heat blazed like an oven.

units.ar: أَقْسَمْتُ بِالْقَمَرِ الْمُنْشَقِّ إِنَّ لَهُ — مِنْ قَلْبِهِ نِسْبَةً مَبْرُورَةَ الْقَسَمِ
units.en: I swear by the cloven moon,—verily, it hath a relation, through his heart, which makes an oath thereby sacred to fulfil,—
units.en2: I swear by the moon split in two — it shares a bond with his heart that makes the oath sacred and binding —

units.ar: وَمَا حَوَى الْغَارُ مِنْ خَيْرٍ وَمِنْ كَرَمٍ — وَكُلُّ طَرْفٍ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ عَنْهُ عَمِي
units.en: And by what the Cave enclosed of good and generous, while all the eyes of the misbelievers were blind thereto,
units.en2: and by the goodness and generosity the Cave held, while every eye of the unbelievers was blind to it:

units.ar: فَالصِّدْقُ فِي الْغَارِ وَالصِّدِّيقُ لَمْ يَرِمَا — وَهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا بِالْغَارِ مِنْ أَرِمِ
units.en: And "Honesty," in the Cave, and the "Vouching Friend" [Abū-Bekr], budged not, while they [their pursuers] were saying: "No soul is in the Cave:"
units.en2: Truthfulness itself and the truest friend did not stir in the Cave, while the pursuers said, "No one is inside."

units.ar: ظَنُّوا الْحَمَامَ وَظَنُّوا الْعَنْكَبُوتَ عَلَى — خَيْرِ الْبَرِيَّةِ لَمْ تَنْسُجْ وَلَمْ تَحُمِ
units.en: They imagined that the Dove would not circle, and they supposed that the Spider would not weave, around the "Best of Mortals;"
units.en2: They thought the dove would not circle and the spider would not weave its web around the Best of Mortals.

units.ar: وِقَايَةُ اللَّهِ أَغْنَتْ عَنْ مُضَاعَفَةٍ — مِنَ الدُّرُوعِ وَعَنْ عَالٍ مِنَ الْأُطُمِ
units.en: The protection of God rendered [them] independent of twofold coats of mail, and of high towers.
units.en2: God's protection made him free of double coats of mail and lofty towers.

units.ar: مَا سَامَنِي الدَّهْرُ ضَيْمًا وَاسْتَجَرْتُ بِهِ — إِلَّا وَنِلْتُ جِوَارًا مِنْهُ لَمْ يُضَمِ
units.en: Time has not offered me an injury [against which] I have had recourse for protection unto him [Muhammad], but I received a protection from him that is not to be infringed;
units.en2: Never has time struck me a blow for which I sought refuge with him, without receiving from him a protection none can breach;

units.ar: وَلَا الْتَمَسْتُ غِنَى الدَّارَيْنِ مِنْ يَدِهِ — إِلَّا اسْتَلَمْتُ النَّدَى مِنْ خَيْرِ مُسْتَلَمِ
units.en: And I have not craved from his hand the riches of this world, or the next, but that I received a bounty from the best of [bestowing hands] respectfully kissed [as their bounty is accepted].
units.en2: and never have I sought from his hand the wealth of this world or the next, without receiving a gift from the noblest of hands ever kissed.

units.ar: لَا تُنْكِرِ الْوَحْيَ مِنْ رُؤْيَاهُ إِنَّ لَهُ — قَلْبًا إِذَا نَامَتِ الْعَيْنَانِ لَمْ يَنَمِ
units.en: Deny thou not the revelation from his vision. Verily he had a heart that did not sleep when the two eyes slept;
units.en2: Do not deny the revelation that came to him in vision — he had a heart that stayed awake when his eyes slept,

units.ar: وَذَاكَ حِينَ بُلُوغٍ مِنْ نُبُوَّتِهِ — فَلَيْسَ يُنْكَرُ فِيهِ حَالُ مُحْتَلِمِ
